page.text:
A proof by cases establishes a conclusion under alternatives whose
disjunction is exhaustive. Each branch inherits the common hypotheses
plus its case assumption. The branches need not be mutually exclusive,
but they must cover every possibility. In constructive arguments, the
cases should also explain how any object claimed to exist is produced in
each branch.
